Selecting or permuting rows and columns

Source: R/matrix.R
tda_msrow.Rd

tda_msrow/tda_mscol select (and may reorder or repeat) rows/columns by index – TDA's msrow/mscol, matching X[rows, ]/X[, cols]. tda_mprow/ tda_mpcol/tda_mpsym permute rows, columns, or both by the same permutation – TDA's mprow/mpcol/ mpsym, matching A[p, ]/A[, p]/A[p, p] (m_mperm's header states the convention, b(i,j)=a(p(i),j) etc.). mprow/mpcol require a permutation of 1:nrow(A)/1:ncol(A), so unlike msrow/ mscol they cannot repeat or drop indices; mpsym additionally requires A to be square.

Usage

tda_msrow(X, rows, dir = tempfile("tda"))

tda_mscol(X, cols, dir = tempfile("tda"))

tda_mprow(A, p, dir = tempfile("tda"))

tda_mpcol(A, p, dir = tempfile("tda"))

tda_mpsym(A, p, dir = tempfile("tda"))

Arguments

X, A

a numeric matrix.

rows, cols

integer indices (1-based; tda_msrow/ tda_mscol allow repeats and omissions).

dir

working directory.

p

an integer permutation of 1:nrow(A) (tda_mprow, tda_mpsym) or 1:ncol(A) (tda_mpcol).

Value

A numeric matrix.

See also

Other matrix reshaping: tda_mag(), tda_mcath(), tda_mcvec(), tda_mrsum(), tda_msort(), tda_mtrim()

Examples

A <- matrix(1:9, 3, 3)
tda_msrow(A, c(2, 1))       # == A[c(2, 1), ]
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    2    5    8
#> [2,]    1    4    7
tda_mprow(A, c(2, 3, 1))    # == A[c(2, 3, 1), ]
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    2    5    8
#> [2,]    3    6    9
#> [3,]    1    4    7
tda_mpsym(A, c(2, 3, 1))    # == A[c(2, 3, 1), c(2, 3, 1)]
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    5    8    2
#> [2,]    6    9    3
#> [3,]    4    7    1
